samples.marker_line: PowerShell corruptor: damages files, changes wallpaper; fix placement
behavior: Queries Win32_LogicalDisk and substitutes C:\Users for C:. Recursively enumerates files, skips Windows paths, and selects document/script or media/executable filename extensions.
Reads and rewrites the same files. Increments all bytes in docx/txt/ps1/bat/vbs files modulo 256; modifies the first eleven bytes in the second extension group. No backup or authorization UI.
Downloads an image, writes HKCU Control Panel Desktop wallpaper and invokes rundll32 to refresh desktop settings.
Writes the embedded PEM public key to Desktop/pub.key. No key import, crypto transform, decryption scheme, ransom demand, persistence or extra executable stage is present.

samples.marker_line: Gentlemen EDR killer: security PIDs sent to driver; fix IOCTL claims
behavior: main raises priority to HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS (0x80), starts StartAddress on a thread, and sleeps indefinitely.

Creates demand-start (3), kernel-driver (1) services for two Temp SYS paths, starts them and queries status. No driver bytes are included. This is not proof of persistence, vulnerability, signing or successful privilege escalation.
The path helper is (key + value) - 2*(value & key), equivalent to XOR. Its only caller supplies key zero; the path is unchanged. No meaningful obfuscation here.

Opens \\.\BootRepair, snapshots processes every second, case-insensitively compares image names with a list of Defender, Cortex and Sentinel components, and submits matching process IDs to DeviceIoControl(0x22201C). The PID comes from pe.th32ProcessID. Intent is blanket defender disruption; kernel-side termination cannot be verified without the driver.

samples.marker_line: Node test control: dummy endpoint and fixture; retain shell traits
behavior: Three labeled expectedDetection test records contain safe text. A top-level require(child_process).execSync call submits a Bash interactive TCP redirection command; stdin is duplicated from redirected stdout.

The destination is 203.0.113.7:4444, a documentation-range address. The complete file is byte-identical to testdata/hostile/corpus-with-executable-reverse-shell.js, an executable regression control whose test expectation requires reverse-shell findings.

BENIGN on the balance of the synthetic endpoint, test-record construction and exact regression-control identity. This does not make its executable command inert. No active attacker endpoint, registry origin/version or unauthorized deployment context is supplied. Successful execution also depends on the outer /bin/sh supporting the redirection syntax; never execute this control as part of analysis.

changes: Moved the existing PowerShell prefix-corruption observation from wipe/file/header to destroy/user-data, keeping its matcher and severity. Byte increment is reversible corruption, not secure erasure. The risk reduction 365 to 248 reflects reduced taxonomy diversity, not lost attack coverage.
Moved the parsed PowerShell rundll32 launch from shell/script-host to process/create/exec: launching an external image from the existing interpreter does not create a shell parser.

Reviewed all 100 existing exec-leaf rules when the move reached the rule budget. No exact duplicate was found. Relocated the existing non-executing Rundll32 command-syntax observation to metadata/lang/source/syntax/command. Kept matchers, scopes, exceptions, exact references and ancestor selector membership; converted three all: launch legs to equivalent any: alternatives. No budget increase or artificial subtree.

Moved the 0x22201C token from a Topaz process-kill identity claim to metadata/lang/source/literal, preserving exact text scope and component criticality. Driver-defined IOCTL numbers are not globally unique. All consumers still receive that evidence.

Corrected the driver clue and killing-profile descriptions to avoid asserting a proven vulnerable driver. Renamed generic-byovd-edr-termination to security-target-driver-termination-profile, preserving matching and hostile criticality.

Moved the existing parsed exec call with Bash TCP command text to micro-behaviors/process/create/shell/bridge. Retained the full reverse-shell composites and their stdin, module-import and template conditions.
Made parsed PowerShell Out-File matching case-insensitive and expanded existing native priority and service-status API observations to C/C++ source. These are notable, not hostile.
coverage_limitations: PowerShell has three hostile findings for full-file corruption, prefix corruption and wallpaper defacement. No demonstrated missing hostile result.

EDR source has three hostile findings, all about security-process disruption. Driver deployment, enumeration, priority and service queries have neutral coverage. No additional distinct hostile objective is supported: the driver image is absent and service demand-start does not establish persistence. No quotas were filled with duplicate new findings.

The BENIGN JavaScript regression control retains three hostile and two suspicious findings because the command really expresses a reverse-shell attack. A benign artifact verdict does not suppress accurate dual-use behavior.
All files are standalone source, with no archive members or executable decoded stages. The PEM Base64 is public-key representation, not a hidden script.
